target_customer: Software companies and developers who need launch videos and marketing creative
problem: Small software teams spend hours in design tools or pay freelancers for marketing content for each release.
business_model: SaaS subscription (free, 39 and 149 USD per month, enterprise custom)
product_category: AI marketing content and product demo video generation

founders.name: Cyrus Kelly
education: University of Adelaide, computer science degree; dropped out of an MBA
previous_startups: communities.one (student club platform, University of Adelaide invested; outcome not found)
founders.background_notes: Started university courses at 13; applied to YC four times per a podcast page.

founders.name: David McDonough
founders.background_notes: Technical lead at VAL.AI, lead engineer at MEQ Solutions.

competitors.name: Arcade
competitors.what: Records real product UI with AI narration into video and interactive demos

competitors.name: Synthesia
competitors.what: Avatar-led AI video for spokesperson and training

technical_complexity.rationale: Orchestrating coding agents, screen capture, voiceover and editing with existing AI APIs; moderate engineering, little original research.

defensibility.rationale: Built on third-party models and standard video tooling; many funded demo tools already exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early to know; funded demo and video tools were already adding AI generation in 2026.

market_need_then: Founders say that across 11 startups they became the marketing team and disliked it; AI coding agents shipping features faster creates a content gap. No spend data found.

branding.domain_note: Owns tday.com; the founders' podcast has chapters on getting the domain, but price and date were not found.

identity.visual_style: Reads customer logo, colors and fonts to produce on-brand output
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, contrasts two minutes with hours in a design tool

brand_strength.rationale: Brand is weeks old; the name is easily confused with the media outlets named TechDay in search results.

outcome_analysis: tday is a Spring 2026 company with two to three founders, an AI coding agent driven demo video product, and no verified funding or exit. The outcome is unknown; crowded demo-video tools and thin defensibility are the visible risks, while the founders' repeated founder experience is the visible strength.
notes: A 500K USD pre-seed in June 2026 appears only on aggregators (FundedIQ, VCBacked) so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. The product pitch on tday.com (narrated demos via coding agents) differs from the YC description (marketing creative and ads), which may indicate a pivot or phased roadmap; no dated source. Team size 2 or 3 depending on source. Outcome search found no news.
